question.text: Which is the primary regulator of mutual funds in India?

answer.text: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)
IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India)
AMFI (Association of Mutual Funds in India)

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) is the primary regulator of mutual funds in India. All mutual fund schemes must be registered with SEBI, and SEBI issued the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996, which serves as the principal regulatory framework. The Trap: RBI regulates banks and monetary policy; IRDAI regulates insurance. AMFI is the industry association of mutual funds whose conduct code and ARN role sit alongside, not in place of, SEBI regulation. Note: For mutual fund grievances, investors can approach SEBI through SCORES; bank-related complaints go to RBI and insurance complaints to IRDAI.
